rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's green depth is the strength of the checks it declares — white means something inside declares none, deeper green means stronger checks, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. It is a promise scale, not results: none of it has run yet. Hover anything for its meaning.

ingest.feed -> ingest.ring — ingest.feed may call ingest.ring. An undeclared cross-component call is flagged as an architecture finding — a warning by default, an error if the calling component is `strict` (§5.3, A0402).

RawFrame data flows from venue to ingest.feed — declared for the picture; nothing checks flows in v1. venue is outside this codebase, so this arrow is a declaration, never a verified fact.

entry — venue can reach Oms::submit from outside this codebase (declared via "entry: [venue]" on Oms::submit). no requires are declared on this function, so it makes no environmental assumption yet. Ply never checks this edge — it is declared, not verified.

venue — a system or person outside this codebase: the exchange: accepts orders, returns fills; market data source. Ply draws it so the boundary is visible, but checks nothing about it — every arrow touching it is a declaration, not a verified fact.
